Automated nightly build from `main` (97d7ab4). These artifacts are unstable and intended for testing only.

🛑 Fixed a data loss bug: the acknowledged LSN could run ahead of the WAL PostgreSQL sent, so a restart skipped committed transactions
* Bump clickhouse/clickhouse-server build image by @dependabot[bot] in https://github.com/xataio/pgstream/pull/1213, https://github.com/xataio/pgstream/pull/1224, https://github.com/xataio/pgstream/pull/1232, https://github.com/xataio/pgstream/pull/1238, https://github.com/xataio/pgstream/pull/1258, https://github.com/xataio/pgstream/pull/1262, https://github.com/xataio/pg

`map` applies the transformer to each element in order and keeps the length. `random` emits between `min_count` and `max_count` elements, each the transform of a source element drawn at random with replacement, so it never invents a value that was not in the row. `min_count` and `max_count` are required with `random`, rejected with `map`, and `max_count` is capped at 10000. Array columns need a source PostgreSQL connection, since the element type is read from the catalog; the connection-less parser rejects

🛂 `pgstream check` no longer fails its `CREATEROLE` check with `database "<role>" does not exist`
🔌 Dropping the database from a connection string no longer drops the user with it, on the `pg_restore --create` path too
* Fix create role check when database is empty by @kvch in https://github.com/xataio/pgstream/pull/1134
* Bump github.com/elastic/go-elasticsearch/v8 from 8.19.6 to 8.19.7 by @dependabot[bot] in https://github.com/xataio/pgstream/pull/1113
* Bump clickhouse/clickhouse-server from 26.7.3

🧬 Replicated `bytea` values are no longer corrupted on the way to a Postgres target

* Bump clickhouse/clickhouse-server from 26.7.2.5

`target.postgres.max_connections` (`PGSTREAM_POSTGRES_WRITER_MAX_CONNECTIONS`) now controls the writer pool size, defaulting to 50 and honoring `pool_max_conns` from the target URL when set explicitly. Previously this setting also sized the schema observer's pool, so a target capped at 90 connections to stay under a 100-connection server limit could still open up to 180. The schema observer is now sized separately, at `min(writer pool, 16)`. So the process now opens at most the configured writer limit plus

`NitroSQLiteQueryResult` no longer extends Nitro's `HybridObject`. Results no longer have `name`, `toString()`, `equals()`, or `dispose()` members from Nitro. Remove result-specific Nitro lifecycle calls and hybrid-object assumptions; ordinary JavaScript garbage collection reclaims results. The data fields `rowsAffected`, `insertId`, `results`, and `metadata` remain, and managed results retain `rows._array`, `rows.length`, and `rows.item()`.

NitroSQLite 10.0.0 is a major release for applications that need more control over SQLite connections and repeated queries. It adds independent database handles, reusable prepared statements, and macOS support for the core and sqlite-vec packages. Async queries, batches, and file imports now enter a native queue without waiting for the previous result to return through JavaScript, while transaction callbacks retain their ordering guarantees.
